ambient_trade.text: Buying salt in {town} at {gold} gold a sack, no less than that :) Caravan leaves at dawn, who wants a share?
Selling iron ingots in {town} for {gold} gold the lot. Fair weight, fair coin, and I mean it :)
Asking {gold} gold for a sound packhorse in {town}. Never sold one at a loss yet and I do not plan to start :)
Who has spare oats in {town}? Paying {gold} gold a measure, cash on the cart, I promise :)
Tolls on the Kashvel road have made salt cost {gold} gold a sack in {town}. Still a fair margin, just barely :)

encounter_trade_offer.text: Ser {player}, I have a cart of iron bound for {town} and I will sell you a share for {gold} gold. Fair prices, I swear it :)
{player}, I am offering {gold} gold for your surplus grain at {town}. Take it or leave it, but the market will not wait :)
{player}, I know our last words were sour. Still, {gold} gold for safe passage through {town} is a deal I would take. Think on it :)
Good to see you again, {player}. Shall we agree on {gold} gold for the salt contract at {town}? Honest weight, honest coin :)
Let us be practical, {player}. I pay {gold} gold a sack at {town} and you save your carts a long walk. Deal? :)

encounter_greeting.text: Ah, {player}! {persona} here, with the wagons of {my_faction} and a fresh tally of salt. Care to trade while the road is quiet? :)
Good day, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, carrying iron down the Kashvel road. Nothing to fear from me, only business :)
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction} here. Our last meeting cost me a cart, so I hope you mean to be civil today :)
{player}! Fancy meeting you on the road. {persona} of {my_faction}, and I have a load that will suit you well :)
Greetings, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, passing through with salt. Fair prices on the road, and no ambush from us :)

player_raided_my_village.text: {village} was burned last night. Whoever did it cost me a season on that road. Nothing personal, just bad for business :(
{player}, you burned {village} and now my carts cannot pass. Ruin helps nobody, not even you. Name your price and let us talk :)
{player}, {village} had grain I was about to buy at a fair price. Think of the coin we both lost, and let us make it right :)
Raiders burned {village} and somebody on this server knows who. Hard to call that good business, is it? :(

war_declared.text: War between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}? Wonderful. Every road closed, every price doubled. Somebody please open the gates :(
{my_faction} has declared war on {enemy_faction}. Bad news for every merchant with a cart. I will be pricing my goods accordingly :)
Sword rattling from {enemy_faction} and now {my_faction} is answering. Cheers, all my salt contracts just went up in smoke :(
Fighting between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} costs us all dearly. Keep clear of the armies and keep trading :)

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last! Roads reopen, the salt carts roll again, and I can finally sleep :)
{my_faction} and {faction} have made peace. Excellent news for the trade routes, and my margins finally breathe :)
Good news from the lords: {my_faction} has signed terms with {faction}. Now let us see the tolls come down :)
A treaty between {my_faction} and {faction}. I drank a toast to it already, and I suggest you do the same :)

released_by_player.text: Released and not ransomed! {player}, you have my thanks and a fair price on my next iron shipment for that kindness :)
Freed by {player} with no ransom asked. That is rare generosity, and I will remember it when the coin changes hands :)
Thank you for the release, {player}. I would have paid a fair ransom, but I am glad to keep my purse closed. Good trade, I say :)
{player} let me go without ransom. Still do not think much of your roads, but the gesture was noted :)
Ransom would have been fairer for both of us, {player}, but I thank you for the release. Perhaps we can talk prices another day :)

beat_by_player.text: Lost {troop_count} men to {player} in the field. Expensive, but a merchant learns the price of every lesson :)
{player}, a field battle with {troop_count} of my men is a poor trade for both of us. Let us talk terms before it costs more :)
Well fought, {player}. We lost {troop_count} men, but I have never walked away from a fair deal and I do not plan to start today :)
Ser {player}, you have taken {troop_count} of my men and I will not pretend I like it. Still, a dead soldier does not pay the toll, so shall we talk? :)
Ser {player}, you beat us fair and square and cost me {troop_count} men. I will buy the next round of salt, and you will get a fair price :)

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {fief} is threatened by {enemy_faction} and my carts are stuck. Lend a few lances and I will pay you well :)
Friend, {enemy_faction} is at my gates in {fief} and the stores are running thin. Help me hold it and I will sell you iron at cost :)
{player}, I am losing ground to {enemy_faction} around {fief}. No profit left to pay soldiers. Could we strike a deal? :)
{fief} may fall to {enemy_faction} unless someone steps in. I cover provisions, you cover swords. Fair terms, I promise :)

ambient_complaint.text: Paid the toll at {town} without a word, as always, and still the bandits on the ridge want a cut. Hell of a road :)
Bandits again on the Kashvel road! Every ambush costs me more than the toll itself. Someone please post guards :)
{rival} is quoting bolts at a loss just to choke the market, and I would rather not say what that does to prices. Bad for everyone :)
{faction} tolls keep climbing every season. A man can pay, but he cannot keep paying forever, can he? :)

ambient_chatter.text: Rain on the road out of {town} again. Mud eats more profit than any bandit, mark my words :)
Stopped at {village} for fresh bread and a cheap ale. Good people, honest prices, a rare find these days :)
Anyone know if the bridge past {village} will hold a laden cart this week? Would hate to lose a load of salt :)
Lag on the server again and I lost a bargain for a wagon of oats. Please tell me someone else was cursed too :)
Sunny days make for good trading. Best time of year to get the roads moving, I think. Anyone else feeling generous? :)
